analysis:
All four units are documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md, docs/developer/test.md). No executable code, keys, wire formats or enforcement paths change in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

What I examined:
- inference.md head lines 5333-5425 cover Qwen27 TP resident assistant, stop ordering and batch arithmetic. The prose describes the existing sealed-collective hidden-row exchange. It also states that public speculative decoding lacks qualification evidence and that a setup saved for coordinator pairing carries no assistant (line 5372). That statement is a conservative scoping that matches TB-011 and T-056 and does not overclaim runtime secrecy or correctness.
- Line 5370 says the saved bilateral policy comes from the native quote, not from a model name. This is consistent with the existing trust-contract model and does not invalidate any assumption.
- The patch excerpt for inference.md also covers the cluster service health-file env handling (partHealthPath vs healthPath, so a part does not overwrite the supervisor heartbeat) and the release-computed cluster_runtime digests. Only prose was supplied; the implementing code and the release lane are not in this batch. The patch also states that an empty or absent health key is passed unchanged. These are integration questions for the code-bearing batches: whether cluster_runtime digest registration changes the approval or attestation trust (TB-011, A-017) and whether heartbeat file separation affects liveness fencing.
- test.md covers the date bump, a new test script entry, and prose describing test rows. The rows include the 128-byte ID limit, the 64 KiB registration cap, the keychain-removed final-app step and a fatal-only-when-send rule. These describe stronger validation, not weaker.

The cache threat T-041 was unaffected: no cache storage, TTL or scope text changed. Prior unrelated claims were not re-verified.

Remaining caveat: the documented behaviors (cluster_runtime release registration, health file split) are implemented in unsupplied files, so I cannot confirm that docs and code match. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a defect.
